description:
Operation is one decision to change one facet of one Stage. Its spec is the
intent and never changes after admission; to change your mind, cancel and
propose again.

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
may reject unrecognized values.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources

kind.description:
Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
Cannot be updated.
In CamelCase.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds

spec.description: OperationSpec is the intent. It is frozen at admission.

actor.description: Actor is the apiserver identity that created the operation.

operation.description: Operation is the uid of the operation that caused this one.

verdict.description: Verdict is one gate's answer plus a citation that can be re-run.

intentDigest.description: IntentDigest is what plan() returned; the promoter recomputes it.

onBehalfOf.description:
Principal is a person an agent says it acts for. It is asserted, never
verified.

params.description:
Params are the operation parameters. On the pointer facet From and To are
OCI manifest digests; on the level facet they are level names.

publisher.description: Publisher is the signer a trust operation asks a person to confirm.

class.description:
ActorClass is who raised an operation, as the promoter classifies the
apiserver identity. It is derived, never asserted by the client.

record.description: Record is the id of the upstream stand-in an acknowledge accepts.

undoes.description: Undoes is the uid of the operation a rollback undoes.

stage.description: Stage is the name of a Stage in the operation's namespace.

witnessed.description:
Witnessed marks an override the promoter raised for an edit it saw but
did not make. Only the promoter may set it.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: an operation's intent is immutable: cancel it and propose again

status.description: OperationStatus is written only by the promoter.

actorClass.description:
ActorClass is who raised an operation, as the promoter classifies the
apiserver identity. It is derived, never asserted by the client.

actorClassifiedBy.description: ActorClassifiedBy is how the actor's class was decided.

applied.description: Applied is true once the pointer moved for this operation.

items.description: ApprovalRecord is an approval the promoter consumed.

access.description:
Access is what let the approver decide, such as
"update deployments/checkout in payments".

accessAt.description: AccessAt is when Access was answered (RFC 3339).

accessSource.description:
AccessSource is who answered Access: subject-access-review or
self-subject-access-review.

classifiedBy.description: ClassifiedBy is how the approver was classified as a person.

decision.description: Decision is what a human approval says.

record.description:
Record is the id of the approval's signed record: the sha256 of its
signed payload.

signer.description: Signer is who signed that record.

onBehalfOf.description: OnBehalfOf is the person a recorder-signed record speaks for.

approvedTeams.description:
ApprovedTeams are the teams the question is asked of (plan.floor.owners)
that an approval counted for since the operation was last held. A change
asked of several teams goes ahead only once every one of them answered.

guarded.description:
Guarded says the promoter found its admission policies guarding the
cluster when it admitted this operation. The promoter admits nothing
otherwise, so it is always true. A record from an earlier promoter or
another cluster may lack it, and its actor and approvers are then only
what their writers claimed.

intentRecord.description:
IntentRecord is the signed record of this operation's intent, written
once the promoter admitted it. Only the recorder writes it.

digest.description: Digest is the record id: the sha256 of its signed payload.

ref.description: Ref is where it is: <repository>@<manifest digest>.

outcome.description: Outcome is how a concluded operation ended.

phase.description: Phase is where an operation is in its lifecycle.

plan.description: Plan is plan()'s answer. It binds to the intent digest.

floor.description:
Floor is the approval floor plan() computed: whether a human must decide,
which decision is asked for and whose.

consumers.description: Consumers are the services that made the floor.

decision.description: Decision is what a human approval says.

owners.description:
Owners are the teams the question is routed to and the only ones whose
members may answer it: the owners of the consumers that made the floor,
or else the team of the Stage's own service. Empty means no team is
declared: nobody may answer when identities.requireOwnerTeam is true
(the default), else any person.

impactDigest.description: ImpactDigest is the sha256 of the pkg/impact answer the floor came from.

order.description:
Order says what must move first when a consumer running in this
environment does not accept the new version. Pacto only says it: it
never moves another service itself.

moveFirst.description:
MoveFirst names every consumer running in this environment whose
declared range does not accept the new version.

items.description: MoveFirst is one consumer that must move before the provider can.

accepts.description: Accepts is the range that version declares on the provider.

candidate.description:
Candidate is the newest version of the consumer its upstream Stage
offered and verified that is newer than the one running here, accepts
both the provider version running here and the new one, accepts what
its other dependencies run here and is accepted by the range every
Pacto here declares on it, so it can move first without breaking a
range Pacto can see. Absent when there is none or Pacto cannot tell.

accepts.description:
Accepts is the range it declares on the provider; empty when it no
longer depends on it.

verifiedOn.description: VerifiedOn is the upstream Stage that verified it.

message.description: Message says all of the above in plain words.

stage.description: Stage is the consumer's Stage in this environment, the one to promote.

unknown.description: Unknown says why Pacto cannot tell whether such a version exists.

version.description:
Version is the consumer version running here that does not accept the
new provider version.

unknown.description:
Unknown says why the list may be incomplete: a partial graph, a range
Pacto cannot read or a consumer it cannot place. Empty means Pacto saw
every consumer running here.

precedent.description:
Precedent is what happened the last times this version was the target
of a recorded operation, on any Stage that attaches records to this
version; a Stage whose registry serves no Referrers API reads only its
own stream. Clients fill it from records;
the promoter leaves it empty.

items.description:
PrecedentEntry is one recorded operation that moved, or tried to move, a
Stage to the version.

outcome.description: Outcome is how a concluded operation ended.

predicted.description: Prediction is what plan() expects the promoter to do.

question.description: Question is the one question a human would be asked.

toVersion.description: ToVersion is the contract service.version of To, when it could be read.

items.description: Verdict is one gate's answer plus a citation that can be re-run.

pointer.description: PointerChange is the pointer before and after an operation.

policy.description:
Policy is the Stage spec the operation concluded under, taken when it
concluded, so its record says what governed it however late it is
written.

applyRef.description:
ApplyRef is the object the promoter points at a version: a Flux
OCIRepository (it sets spec.ref.digest) or an Argo CD Application (it
sets spec.source.targetRevision). Nothing else is ever written on it.

kind.description:
Kind is OCIRepository (Flux, the default), Application (Argo CD, with
an OCI source and automated sync) or HelmRelease (Flux: the promoter
writes the chart digest on the OCIRepository its spec.chartRef names).

approval.description: ApprovalPolicy can only raise the approval floor, never lower it.

always.description: Always holds every promote for a human, whatever the contracts say.

autonomy.description: AutonomyPolicy tunes when Pacto proposes the next level.

proposeAfter.description: ProposeAfter is how many qualifying promotions earn a proposal.

candidates.description:
Candidates says where new versions come from. At most one of registry,
ociRepositoryRef, upstreamStage and upstreamRecords is set, so the version
offered and the version judged come from the same source; a Stage that sets
none is not Ready and never promotes.

ociRepositoryRef.description:
OCIRepositoryRef is a Flux OCIRepository the promoter only reads: the
candidate is the @sha256: part of its status.artifact.revision.

registry.description:
Registry is the promoter's own registry watch: a new version tag is
a candidate once its Sigstore signature comes from a publisher the
promoter's publisher rule accepts (delivery.publishers).

repository.description:
Repository (host/path) is the repository watched; empty watches the
repository the Stage's applier takes versions from.

upstreamRecords.description:
UpstreamRecords offers what a Stage in another cluster verified, read
from its signed records: the promoter must trust the key that signs
that stream (promoter.upstreamTrust), or it offers nothing.

repository.description: Repository (host/path) is the upstream recorder's streams repository.

stream.description:
Stream is the upstream Stage's stream id, <clusterID>/<namespace>/<name>:
its status.stream.id.

upstreamStage.description: UpstreamStage offers that Stage's verified digests minus its failed ones.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: set at most one of candidates.registry, candidates.ociRepositoryRef, candidates.upstreamStage and candidates.upstreamRecords

deadlines.description: Deadlines override the operation type's defaults (Go durations).

environment.description:
Environment is the environment the Stage delivers to, such as prod.
A promote matches it against the environments the version's contract
declares (environments[].name): a contract that declares environments
must declare this one, with values that satisfy its configuration
schemas, or the promote waits for a person (pacto.environment). It
also places the Pactos and Stages a change's consumers run on, and
selects the values the applier may apply: values-<environment>.yaml or
overlays/<environment>. It is fixed at creation.

gates.description:
Gates configures the Stage's gates. The pre-gates are fixed by the operation
type; the Pacto contract check always verifies, beside the Stage's checks.

declaredConsumersOnly.description:
DeclaredConsumersOnly says every consumer of the service has a
contract Pacto can see, so a breaking change no Pacto depends on ships
without a person. Off by default: a service with no contract can still call it, so
a breaking change with no consumer in sight waits for a person to accept
the unknown.

verify.description: VerifyGates configures what runs after a version is applied.

checks.description:
Checks are this Stage's own verify gates, run beside the Pacto contract
check: a health provider set in delivery.gates.providers, or the built-in
pacto.runtime claim gate.

items.description: GateCheck is one verify gate a Stage runs.

name.description: Name is the gate id its verdicts carry, unique on the Stage.

params.description: Params are the provider's settings (thresholds, filters).

provider.description:
Provider is a gate provider set in delivery.gates.providers, or
pacto.runtime. A Stage cannot name a URL: providers are operator
configuration.

requireObservedModel.description:
RequireObservedModel makes an eval check Unknown unless its runner
says which model answered (observedModel) and the contract declares
an external dependency with a version to compare it with. A model the
runner names that no such version matches fails the check either way.

suite.description:
Suite names a check the version's contract ships (its checks[].name)
for an eval provider to run; without it the provider runs the only check
the version ships. A version whose contract ships no check of that name,
or with no suite ships none or more than one, is held for a person
before it ships.

suiteDigest.description:
SuiteDigest pins the suite's bytes ("sha256:" and 64 hex digits). A
version whose suite has another digest changed its own exam: it is held
for a person before it ships, and an eval check of it is Unknown.

recheck.description:
Recheck is how often the verify gates run again on the version the
Stage runs once it shipped (a Go duration, default 1m). A confirmed Fail
rolls it back; Unknown never does.

window.description:
Window is how long the verify gates may stay Unknown before the
operation is held for a human (a Go duration, default 5m). Re-checks
after release judge the same length of time.

records.description:
RecordsPolicy says whether automation may move the Stage while its records
cannot be written.

required.description:
Required holds every promote or rollback an agent or the promoter
raises for a person to approve while the recorder is not writing this
Stage's records (RecordStoreReady is not True) or more than five of
its operations wait for a record (MaxRecordsPending).

service.description:
ServiceRef is the Pacto ServiceID a Stage delivers: the domain-qualified
service name its contracts declare.

domain.description: Domain is the registry and organisation scope (empty for the default).

startLevel.description:
StartLevel is where a new Stage begins. It is read once, when
status.level is empty; after that only an autonomy operation moves the
level. Creating a Stage is an admin action, so any level is accepted, and
a Stage whose status is lost seeds back to this level. Only observe and
advise keep Pacto from shipping without a person.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: startLevel is fixed at creation; propose delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/autonomy to change the level

workload.description:
Workload is the workload the service runs as, in the Stage's namespace:
the one object pacto.contract and pacto.runtime may judge. The Pacto
resource ships inside every version and names its own target, so
without this a version could point its own check at a decoy. Empty is
the Deployment named spec.service.name.

kind.description: Kind is the workload kind, such as Deployment or StatefulSet.

question.description: Question is what a human is asked while the operation is Held.

reason.description:
Reason is the machine reason for the outcome or the hold (PlanStale,
PointerMoved, NoStage, ...).

record.description:
Record is the signed record of this operation, once the recorder wrote
it. Only the recorder writes it.

digest.description: Digest is the record id: the sha256 of its signed payload.

kind.description: Kind is operation, or unrecordable when a pre-sign check refused it.

refused.description: Refused names the check and why, for an unrecordable record.

seq.description: Seq is the record's place in the stream.

stageUID.description:
StageUID is the uid of the Stage that gave the operation its seq. A
Stage deleted and recreated with the same name starts its seqs over,
and an operation left over from the old one is not part of the new one.

held.description:
Held is when the operation was last held for a person. An approval
created before it answered an earlier question and does not count.

items.description: Verdict is one gate's answer plus a citation that can be re-run.
